clue.text: Man who does cartoons about Communist city in North Italy is permanently traumatized

indicators.note: the cartoonist's name goes around the other pieces, so about signals that it surrounds them

parts.note: Gerald Scarfe is a well-known British cartoonist
a Communist is called a Red
Forli is a city in Emilia-Romagna, northern Italy

explanation.surface: A satirical cartoonist's portrayal of a Red city in northern Italy leaves someone deeply damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means the cartoonist's surname is split open to take in the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone left with lasting emotional damage is said to be scarred in that way for good.

clue.text: See 10
Specific commercial for wine, say

parts.note: an ad is a commercial or advertisement

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, so only its sound counts

parts.note: hock is a white German wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A clue about a particular advertisement promoting wine.
explanation.walkthrough: HOCK, a British name for Rhine wine, sounds like HOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase meaning arranged for one particular purpose, so special or specific rather than general.

clue.text: Teller of tales disturbs our trance

indicators.note: to disturb is to throw out of order, so the letters of our trance get rearranged

explanation.surface: A storyteller breaks the hypnotic spell an audience has fallen into.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled storyteller, especially one who tells anecdotes well in conversation.

clue.text: 23's game with foam turning into strange fluid

indicators.note: the game and the shuffled foam are put inside the other letters, so into marks the container
strange suggests something odd or altered, so the letters of fluid are rearranged

parts.note: chess is a board game

indicators.note: turning suggests churning over, so the letters of foam are rearranged

explanation.surface: A game played while foam churns into some odd liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is the playwright, so '23's' means a play of his. 'strange' gives DULFI, which 'into' splits around the game and OFMA (from 'turning').
explanation.definitionFit: The Duchess of Malfi is the best-known tragedy by the Jacobean playwright John Webster.

clue.text: See 4
Extraction of oscillating tongue

indicators.note: an extraction is something drawn out, so the answer is taken out of the following word

explanation.surface: Removing something that keeps swinging back and forth from someone's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue here means a language, and Latin is the language of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Proper person to make a catalogue

parts.note: to form something is to make it
a list is a catalogue of items

explanation.surface: A stickler for correctness is the sort to draw up an inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: A formalist insists strictly on correct forms and rules, so is a very proper sort.

clue.text: Morality in Lambeth? I can't believe it

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words Lambeth? I can't, running across them

explanation.surface: Someone expresses disbelief that moral standards exist in a London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambeth is a London borough, home to the Archbishop of Canterbury's palace.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral principle or set of moral values governing conduct.

clue.text: Energy went with ecstasy in call from graveyard

indicators.note: in places the first three pieces inside the call

parts.note: a cry is a call or shout
E is the physics symbol for energy
met, as in went to meet or met up with
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A ghostly cry from a burial ground, full of energy and rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cemetery is a burial ground, another word for a graveyard.

clue.text: 4 5's epitaph by chap at contest in which he has heartless referee born by agreement with lawman in Scotch mist at an outbuilding that's got non-U solvers into muck

parts.note: cove is old slang for a chap

indicators.note: the contest has the next pieces put within it

parts.note: a race is a contest
taken as written

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of referee goes
in places the next three pieces inside the Scottish drizzle

parts.note: mizzle is a fine misty drizzle, as in Scotch mist
nee means born, used before a maiden name
yes expresses agreement
DA is a district attorney, a US lawman
a shed is an outbuilding
ie, from Latin id est, means that is

indicators.note: into puts the shortened solvers inside the muck

parts.note: dung is muck or manure

indicators.note: non-U means without the letter U

parts.note: the setter addresses the solvers as you

explanation.surface: A rambling tale of a man at a contest, a referee, a lawman in the mist and solvers dropped in muck.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 5 is THE DUCHESS OF MALFI; Ferdinand's line over his dead sister serves as her epitaph. 'heartless' makes RF from REF; 'non-U' makes YO from YOU. 'by', 'with', 'at an' and 'got' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand speaks these words over his murdered sister's body in Webster's tragedy, and they serve as her memorial line.

clue.text: Make cross with holy smoke

definitions.meaning: to make someone angry or enraged, a verb stressed on the second syllable
fragrant smoke from burnt spices used in religious ritual

explanation.surface: Angering someone by wafting church smoke at them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning to enrage and a noun for sweet-smelling smoke burnt in worship.

clue.text: See about continuing joke from the distant past

indicators.note: the word for see goes about the other pieces, surrounding them

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
on, as in carrying on
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: Look at this running joke dating from ages back.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes something belonging to times far back, an idiom for the remote past.

clue.text: He wrote in French of the person he fought

parts.note: de is the French word for of
a foe is an enemy, someone fought against

explanation.surface: A writer composed in French about his enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: 'He wrote in' French reads naturally but 'in' simply joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the English writer of Robinson Crusoe, so a man who wrote.

clue.text: I reduced time when climbing in marshland — I must have pasta

indicators.note: in places the climbing pieces inside the marshland

parts.note: a fen is an area of marshland in eastern England

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the pieces are written backwards

parts.note: to cut is to reduce

explanation.surface: Someone trims their schedule while hiking through a bog and insists on a pasta meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when climbing' turns the three pieces into TTUCI, which 'in' puts inside the marsh; the second I follows, 'must have' being a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fettucini are flat ribbon noodles, a type of Italian pasta.

clue.text: Punish severely for breaking nail during evasion of work

indicators.note: during places the broken nail inside the word for shirking

parts.note: to skive is British slang for dodging work

indicators.note: breaking suggests smashing up, so the letters of nail are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boss threatens harsh punishment for a worker who broke a nail while skiving.
explanation.walkthrough: SKIVE is British slang for shirking work; NALI (rearranged nail) sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To flay someone alive is a hyperbolic idiom for punishing or scolding them harshly.

clue.text: A vague chat includes "down with Canadian lake"

indicators.note: includes means the shuffled chat contains the French phrase
vague suggests something blurred and unclear, so the letters of chat get rearranged

parts.note: a bas is French for down with

explanation.surface: An aimless conversation features a protest cry against a Canadian lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vague' gives THCA, which 'includes' splits around the French slogan à bas.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Athabasca lies on the border of Alberta and Saskatchewan in Canada.

clue.text: Extreme East German following Hilary, for example

indicators.note: following means the German word comes after the other piece

parts.note: Hilary is the spring term at Oxford University, an OU term
Ost is German for east

explanation.surface: A remark that an East German came after an Oxford don named Hilary.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary term is the spring term at Oxford, so 'Hilary, for example' is an OU (Oxford University) TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: Outermost means furthest out, at the extreme edge.

clue.text: Spend too much and you get worried about part of speech

indicators.note: about places the shuffled you around the part of speech
worried suggests being shaken about, so the letters of you are rearranged

parts.note: a verb is a part of speech in grammar

explanation.surface: Overspending leaves a shopper anxious about what to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' gives OUY, which 'about' splits around the part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbuy is to purchase more than needed, spending excessively.

clue.text: In the direction of conflict among foxes

indicators.note: among means the conflict sits inside the foxes

parts.note: tod is a dialect word for a fox
a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: Heading towards a fight breaking out among a group of foxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A preposition meaning heading for, or in the direction of.

clue.text: Something wrong? Get another driver

definitions.meaning: a snag or problem that holds things up
to thumb a lift from a passing motorist

explanation.surface: A motorist's car breaks down and they look for a replacement chauffeur.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a snag and a verb for hitch-hiking with a passing motorist.

clue.text: Some you can hear on your own in a cell

parts.note: N stands for an indefinite number, so some

indicators.note: you can hear means the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: taken by sound, your own runs together

explanation.surface: Advice that some sounds are only audible while alone in a cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link; 'in' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurone is a nerve cell, the basic unit of the nervous system.

clue.text: Cat's weight

definitions.meaning: the snow leopard, a big cat of Central Asia
an imperial unit of weight, one sixteenth of a pound

explanation.surface: A question of how heavy a cat is.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the snow leopard and a small imperial unit of weight.

clue.text: Playwright who uses the Internet?

definitions.meaning: a whimsical coinage for someone using the ... as in trickster

explanation.surface: A dramatist who goes online.
explanation.definitionFit: John Webster was a Jacobean playwright, and the word also reads as a jokey term for a web user.

clue.text: Stone of supreme extremes

parts.note: top means best or supreme
A and Z are the extremes of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A gem of the very highest quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a gemstone, a precious stone usually yellow.

clue.text: Shedder of Caesar's blood other than vermilion

parts.note: Cinna was one of the conspirators who stabbed Julius Caesar
bar means except or other than

explanation.surface: An assassin of Caesar is identified as anything but red.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is the mineral mercury sulphide, the source of the bright red pigment vermilion.

clue.text: Photographers' ink?

parts.note: a cuttlefish's dark ink lends its name to the brown tint of old photographs

explanation.surface: Asking what pigment photographers use.
explanation.definitionFit: The brown pigment from cuttlefish ink also names the brownish tone of old photographs.
